This publication is part of the WHO guideline titled WHO Recommendations: Uterotonics for the Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage. It is made publicly available for transparency and informational purposes, as required by WHO guidelines. The document includes evidence-based recommendations on the use of uterotonic agents (e.g., oxytocin, carbetocin, misoprostol, ergometrine, injectable prostaglandins, and combinations such as oxytocin plus ergometrine or misoprostol plus oxytocin) for preventing postpartum hemorrhage (PPH). The recommendations are based on a network meta-analysis of 196 trials involving 135,559 women across 53 countries. Oxytocin was the reference uterotonic agent in one-third of the trials and was the most frequently investigated agent. The analysis found no significant differences in maternal death rates between uterotonic agents and placebo, as maternal death was a rare outcome. Similarly, no uterotonic agent was found to be more effective than oxytocin in preventing PPH ≥ 1000 mL. Evidence for carbetocin and injectable prostaglandins was uncertain. For severe maternal morbidity, such as ICU admission, no detectable differences were observed among uterotonic agents, although evidence for some agents (e.g., ergometrine, oxytocin plus ergometrine, and misoprostol plus oxytocin) was of very low certainty. Regarding postpartum anemia, evidence on mean changes in hemoglobin levels before and after birth was limited. Misoprostol and injectable prostaglandins showed unclear effects due to very low-certainty evidence. Side effects such as vomiting, headache, abdominal pain, fever, and diarrhea were reported, with varying levels of certainty about their association with specific uterotonic agents. Subgroup analyses did not reveal substantial differences in the effects of uterotonic agents based on the mode of birth (vaginal vs. cesarean section) or setting (community vs. hospital). The desirable and undesirable effects of different uterotonic agents were assessed, with oxytocin serving as the reference agent.
